root_cause: The fast-path regex _is_single_cell_widths in rich/cells.py was '^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$': the ASCII range stopped at U+006F ('o') instead of U+007E ('~'), so p-z and {|}~ missed the fast path, and '\u00a0\u02ff' lacked a hyphen, so it matched two single code points instead of the Latin-1/Latin-Extended range. Strings with those characters fell to the slow per-character width path (a performance bug, not a correctness bug).
best_solution: Rewrite the character class to '^[\u0020-\u007e\u00a0-\u02ff\u0370-\u0482\u2500-\u25FF]*$': end printable ASCII at '~' (U+007E, excluding DEL), add the missing hyphen so U+00A0-U+02FF is a range, and add U+2500-U+25FF (box drawing, block elements, geometric shapes), which rich draws constantly in tables and panels and which are all 1 cell wide. The gold patch also adds 'assert cut >= 0' and an Args docstring to Segment.split_cells (not tested). Reasoning path from the statement: read every range in the class, check each against the width table (every char in range must have cell width 1), then add the most common single-width characters in the library's own output.
acceptable_alternatives: Any class that matches every printable ASCII char (0x20-0x7e), every char of U+2500-U+257F box drawing (at least the ones in the test string), and still rejects emoji and CJK (e.g. わさび, 💩). Keeping or dropping DEL (0x7f) does not matter to the test. Including a wider range verified to be all width-1 against CELL_WIDTHS would also pass.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_is_single_cell_widths imports _is_single_cell_widths from rich.cells and asserts: truthy for every string.printable char with ord>=32; truthy for each char of the box string '┌─┬┐│ ││├─┼┤...└─┴┘' (U+2500 block); falsy for '💩😽' and for 'わさび'. The box-drawing requirement is not in the statement.
locating_signals: Statement says 'regex used to select the fast path for strings with single-width characters'. Grepping for 'single' or 're.compile' in rich/ finds _is_single_cell_widths in rich/cells.py right away. The function is not named in the statement, but only one regex fits.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4, v6 and v7 produced empty patches after 64-85 calls and 366-500 s. v8 (87 s, 51 calls) found the right line but only changed \u006f to \u007f: it left out the missing hyphen in '\u00a0\u02ff' and did not add the box-drawing range, so the hidden test failed on _is_single_cell_widths('┌') returning None. Even with the hyphen fixed it would have failed, because the box-drawing requirement exists only in the test.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says a regex or character class is 'wrong', audit every token in the class, not just the first suspicious endpoint: check each range's endpoints against the intended set, look for missing '-' between code points, and check each bound against the ground-truth function (here: loop over the range and assert the slow-path width function returns 1). Then write a quick membership test over representative inputs, including the characters the library itself emits most (for a terminal renderer, box-drawing chars). If a fast path is supposed to mirror a slow path, test that it agrees with the slow path. Also: an empty patch always scores zero, so once the location is found, commit a best-effort edit early instead of exploring until the budget runs out.
